papers.title: Weaken to Strengthen: Weakening-Induced On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Reasoning Models
papers.problem: Reasoning models cannot improve themselves without a stronger teacher or extra answer labels.
papers.fix: Training a model against a deliberately weakened copy raised average accuracy by 4.0 points (quantized) and 5.5 points (pruned).
papers.practicalUseCase: A model can teach itself without labels, so cheap self-training on your own prompts may lift reasoning accuracy.
papers.limitation: Tests covered math and coding benchmarks only.

papers.title: Unlocking Any-Order Generation in Pretrained Autoregressive Image Models
papers.problem: Image generators trained in one fixed pixel order cannot fill in or edit parts of an image.
papers.fix: A small retraining recipe gave inpainting a score of 6.21 versus 10.44 for MaskGIT, at 13-33% extra compute.
papers.practicalUseCase: You can add editing to an existing image model cheaply, so skip training a new one from scratch.
papers.limitation: Normal image quality gets slightly worse, with scores 1.2 to 1.9 higher.

papers.title: Matched Capabilities, Different Behaviors: A Controlled Study of MCP and CLI Interfaces for Language Agents
papers.problem: The same agent tools shown as MCP or as command line can make agents behave very differently.
papers.fix: Matched MCP and CLI interfaces gave very different task scores, and paths diverged in 94.3% of 2,004 episodes.
papers.practicalUseCase: Interface design changes agent results, so test both forms of your tools before you blame the model.
papers.limitation: Tests used six models and three environments, so other setups may differ.

papers.title: Broken on Arrival: Non-Functional Quantized LLM Artifacts in Public Model Registries and How to Catch Them
papers.problem: Public model registries never test whether downloaded low-bit code models still work.
papers.fix: Seven of 305 official Ollama tags (2.3%) solved at most six of 164 tasks, all small low-bit models.
papers.practicalUseCase: Some small quantized models arrive broken, so run a quick code test before you trust a download.
papers.limitation: Only some official tags and 22 community files were checked, so other registries may differ.

papers.title: EPSBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Earnings Forecasting
papers.problem: AI agents struggle to forecast company earnings from filings, call transcripts, and news.
papers.fix: Three of six models matched analyst consensus, but their 80% intervals held the true earnings only 37-70% of the time.
papers.practicalUseCase: Agent forecasts look sure but miss often, so do not trust their stated confidence ranges for money decisions.
papers.limitation: Results cover 149 firm-quarters from 86 US companies and six models.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks set up sustainability committees, but nobody knew if committees change environmental results in dual banking systems.
papers.fix: Committees raised overall environmental scores, but in Islamic banks they moved only overall and resource scores, not products or innovation.
papers.practicalUseCase: Committees in Islamic banks may be mostly for show, so check for real green products before you trust the label.
papers.limitation: Panel regressions show links between committees and scores, not cause.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Sustainability sukuk are growing fast, yet nobody had mapped what drives how big each issue is.
papers.fix: Across 11,944 issues, growth sits in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Saudi Arabia, and equity-based contracts give larger issues.
papers.practicalUseCase: Contract type and costly outside reviews shape issue size, so issuers should favor equity-based contracts and watch review costs.
papers.limitation: Data end in 2022 and show patterns, not cause.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic banks in Jordan lacked proof that AI and big data actually help them compete.
papers.fix: AI use, big data skills, and data management all link positively to competitiveness and sustainable development in 214 surveyed managers.
papers.practicalUseCase: Data and AI investment goes with stronger banks, so Islamic banks should fund both before they chase other upgrades.
papers.limitation: A single-time survey of Jordanian managers shows links, not cause.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Nobody knew which national forces make banks grow in systems with both Islamic and conventional banks.
papers.fix: ICT adoption drove growth most across 218 banks in 12 countries, and high-tech exports helped only alongside ICT.
papers.practicalUseCase: Digital tools drive bank growth more than anything else tested, so invest in digital infrastructure first.
papers.limitation: Data cover 12 countries from 2010 to 2023 and show links, not cause.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Islamic finance grew fast, yet many people in Muslim-majority countries still lack financial services.
papers.fix: Income, tertiary education, institutions, internet access, population, and age dependency drive inclusion across 35 OIC and OECD countries.
papers.practicalUseCase: OIC countries need digital infrastructure and youth and women support, so these pay off more than copying OECD policy.
papers.limitation: Country-level data from 2005 to 2021 show links, not cause.

papers.title: Global prevalence of impostor phenomenon in medical students: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.institution: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza
papers.problem: Medical students face constant tests and comparison, but nobody had pooled how often they feel like frauds.
papers.fix: Impostor feelings were frequent among medical students worldwide, though results varied widely by sampling method and region.
papers.practicalUseCase: Many high achievers feel like frauds, so expect it in tough training and talk about it early.
papers.limitation: Studies differed a lot, so the pooled rate is uncertain.

papers.title: What keeps gig workers motivated? A typology of the intrinsic-extrinsic motivation interplay in the digital gig economy
papers.institution: Sri Lanka Institute of Information Technology
papers.problem: Nobody knew how inner drive and pay pressure mix to keep gig workers engaged on digital platforms.
papers.fix: Gig workers show different motivation profiles, and digital skills link motivation to engagement.
papers.practicalUseCase: Digital skills turn motivation into steady work, so build platform skills along with chasing pay.
papers.limitation: Only Sri Lankan platform workers were studied, mostly young part-timers.

papers.title: Exploring the influencing factors of academic doctoral students’ academic innovation behavior in the context of generative artificial intelligence: Self-determination theory and motivation-opportunity-ability perspectives
papers.problem: Doctoral students may use generative AI in research, but the drivers of their new ideas were unclear.
papers.fix: Inner and outer motivation both push new ideas together, but long unmet psychological needs sharply cut innovation.
papers.practicalUseCase: Unmet needs kill creative research, so protect autonomy and support before adding more AI tools.
papers.limitation: A single-time self-report survey of chemistry students cannot prove cause.
